pairs.label: kw-01/relevant
pairs.document: A dead letter exchange receives messages that were rejected without requeue, that expired, or that overflowed a queue length limit. A queue is wired to it with the x-dead-letter-exchange argument. Operators bind a dead letter queue to the exchange and inspect it to find poison messages: payloads that fail every time and would otherwise cycle forever. The dead letter queue keeps the evidence for later replay.

pairs.label: kw-01/irrelevant
pairs.document: With manual acknowledgements a consumer tells RabbitMQ when a delivery was handled. BasicAckAsync removes the message from the queue. BasicNackAsync with requeue set to true puts the message back so another attempt can happen, while requeue set to false discards it or routes it to a dead letter exchange. If a consumer crashes before acknowledging, the broker redelivers the message, which is why handlers must tolerate duplicates.

pairs.label: pa-01/irrelevant
pairs.query: what happens to messages that keep failing forever
pairs.document: Prefetch limits how many unacknowledged deliveries a consumer may hold. A prefetch count of 8 means the broker stops sending after eight messages are in flight until some are acknowledged. This is the main backpressure mechanism: slow workers stay bounded instead of buffering the entire queue in memory, and unacked messages remain available for other consumers.

pairs.label: pa-06/relevant
pairs.query: combining two ranked result lists without comparing their scores
pairs.document: Reciprocal rank fusion adds 1 divided by k plus rank for every list in which a document appears. The constant k is conventionally 60 and dampens the advantage of the very top ranks. Because only ranks are used, no score normalisation is needed, and a document found by both retrievers rises above documents found by one.

pairs.label: mr-01/relevant
pairs.query: reduce the cost of calling the embedding API
pairs.document: Embedding the same text twice is wasted money, so systems cache vectors under a hash of the text and the model name. Because an embedding is a pure function of model and text, such entries never go stale and only need a TTL for memory hygiene. Storing floats as raw bytes is far smaller than JSON.

pairs.label: co-02/relevant
pairs.query: restricting vector search to documents with a given attribute
pairs.document: Qdrant applies payload filters during graph traversal rather than after it. A filter has must, should and must_not clauses; a match condition on a keyword field restricts candidates to points whose payload equals the value. Because filtering happens inside the search, asking for ten results with a selective filter still returns ten results instead of an empty page, provided enough points match.
